chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Marwazi al-Muqri said: Abu 'Amr Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Muqri said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Musili said in Baghdad that Muhammad ibn 'Asim al-Tarifi said: 'Ayyash ibn Yazid ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Kahhal, the freed slave of Zayd ibn 'Ali, said: My father related to me that Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them) related to me that a group of people said to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): 'We supplicate but our supplication is not answered,'
He (peace be upon him) responded: 'Because you supplicate to One whom you do not truly recognize.'

key_terms.الصادق: Al-Sadiq (The Truthful), title of Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad

ai.seo_question: Why are our prayers not answered according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the root cause of unanswered supplication as a deficiency in *ma'rifah* (gnostic recognition) of the Divine. This highlights the Shia theological principle that effective invocation requires not merely verbal address, but an intimate, knowledgeable awareness of God’s attributes and presence, aligning with the chapter’s theme that God is known only through His own self-revelation.
